title: VOR
src: R.K. Bali — Air Navigation, Part III Ch 4 (key read from the printed answer grid, PDF p. 256; Q2–3 are worked examples turned into choices)

qs.q: Which of the following would not trigger the warning flag on VOR indicators?
An aircraft at 40 000 ft; the VOR elevation is 900 ft. Up to what range can the VOR signal be received?
An aircraft at FL400; the VOR is at MSL. Maximum reception range?
What is the minimum level that an aircraft, at a range of 113NM, must fly in order to contact the tower on R/T for a VDF bearing from an airport sited 169ft above MSL?
What is the approximate maximum theoretical range at which an aircraft at FL130 could receive information from a VDF facility which is sited 1024ft above MSL?
The maximum theoretical range at which an aircraft at FL.80 can obtain bearings from a ground VDF facility sited at 325ft above MSL is:
A VOR receiver check can be made
o: At designated check point on airport surface
Any where in the air/ ground

qs.q: DVOR works on the principle of
o: Measuring Doppler frequency shift between fixed and variable signal
Measuring phase difference between fixed and variable signal
Measuring time difference induced by Doppler frequency shift in single signal

An omni-bearing selector (OBS) shows full deflection to the left when within range of a serviceable VOR. What angular deviation are you from the selected radial?
qs.ex: Full-scale deflection on a VOR CDI is 10° (5 dots × 2°).

qs.q: The two signals transmitted by a conventional VOR ground station are 90" out of phase on magnetic:
The frequency range of a VOR receiver is:
VOR station position N61°E025, variation 13"E; Estimated position of an aircraft N59°E025°, variation 20°E. What VOR radial is the aircraft on?
qs.ex: The aircraft is due south (180° T). Radials use the variation at the VOR: 180 − 13 E = 167.

qs.q: Which of the following statements concerning the variable, or directional, signal of a conventional VOR is correct?
o: The receiver adds 30Hz to the variable signal before combining it with the reference signal
The transmitter changes the frequency of the variable signal by 30Hz either side of the allocated frequency each time it rotates
The rotation of the variable signal at a rate of 30 times per second gives it the characteristics of a 30Hz amplitude modulation

qs.q: In which frequency band do VOR transmitters operate?
If the reference phase differs by 30° from the variable phase, the radial from the VOR station will be:
In order to plot a bearing from a VOR station, a pilot needs to know the magnetic variation:
o: at the half-way point between the aircraft and the station

qs.q: A VOR is sited at position A(45°00'N, 010°00'E). An aircraft is located at position B(44°00'N, 010°00'E). Assuming that the magnetic variation at A is 10°W and at B is 15°W, the aircraft is on VOR radial:
qs.ex: Due south of the VOR: 180° T + 10° W (VOR variation) = 190.

qs.q: An aircraft is flying on true track 090° towards a VOR near the equator where the magnetic variation is 15° E. The variation at the aircraft position is 8° E. The aircraft is on VOR radial:
qs.ex: The aircraft is west of the VOR: 270° T − 15° E (VOR variation) = 255.

qs.q: The principle used in VOR bearing measurement is:
Transmissions from VOR facilities may be adversely affected by:
o: uneven propagation over irregular ground surfaces

qs.q: If VOR bearing information is used beyond the published protection range, errors could be caused by:
o: noise from precipitation static exceeding the signal strength of the transmitter
sky wave interference from distant transmitters on the same frequency

qs.q: An airway 10NM wide is to be defined by two VORs each having a resultant bearing accuracy of plus or minus 5.5°. In order to ensure accurate track guidance within the airway limits the maximum distance apart for the transmitter is approximately:
qs.ex: Half-width 5 NM ÷ tan 5.5° ≈ 52 NM from each VOR: about 105 NM apart.

qs.q: The VOR system is limited to about 1° of accuracy. One degree at 200NM represents a width of:
An aircraft is required to approach a VOR via the 104° radial. Which of the following settings should be made on the VOR/ILS deviation indicator?

An aircraft on a heading of 280°(M) is on a bearing of 090°(M) from a VOR. The bearing you should select on the OMNI bearing selector to centralise the VOR/ILS left/right deviation needle with a "TO" indication is:
qs.ex: Bearing 090° from the VOR means the aircraft is on the 090 radial; to go TO the station select 270.

qs.q: An aircraft is required to approach a VOR station via the 244° radial. In order to obtain correct sense indications the deviation indicator should be set to:

An aircraft is 100NM from a VOR facility. Assuming no error when using a deviation indicator where 1 dot= 2° deviation, how many dots deviation from the center line of the instrument will represent the limits of the airway boundary? (Assume that the airway is 10NM wide.)
qs.ex: 5 NM at 100 NM = 3°; at 2° per dot that is 1.5 dots.

qs.q: The TO/FROM indicator of a VOR:
o: Tells whether a track equal to the selected bearing will bring you to or away from the VOR
Tells whether you are now flying towards or from the VOR
Tells whether you should turn the aircraft towards or away from the CDI indication

qs.q: An aircraft is tracking inbound to a VOR beacon on the 105 radial. The setting the pilot should put on the OBS and the CDI indications are:
The principle advantage of Doppler VOR is that:
o: a readout of range as well as bearing is obtained

qs.q: When a maximum range and altitude is published for a VOR?
o: The terrain will cause bends and/or scalloping on the VOR signal and make it inaccurate outside standards in the airspace outside the published airspace
The reception from this VOR is guaranteed free from harmful interference from other VORs when you are within this airspace
The signal from the VOR will be too weak to provide information when you are outside this airspace

qs.q: An aircraft is over flying a VOR at 30,000 ft, at a groundspeed of 300 kt. The maximum time during which no usable signals will be received (in minutes and seconds) is:
During maintenance, malfunction or testing the identification signal of a VOR transmitter is (i) by (ii) or (iii).
o: Suppressed; by a modulated tone; or suppression
Suppressed; by a continuous tone; or removed
Replaced; by a continuous tone; or Morse letter S

qs.q: For an aircraft at 30,000 ft what is the maximum radius above a VOR where unreliable or no signals at all may be received at 45° above horizontal :
qs.ex: 30 000 ft ≈ 5 NM; at 45° the radius equals the height: 5 NM.
